newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hajdutej export subsidies cut hurts profit.
newsitem.headline: Hajdutej export subsidies cut hurts profit.

text.p: Hungarian dairy company Hajdutej Rt said on Monday that its 1996 sales of 11.32 billion forints were in line with its plans, while its operating profit fell as export subsidies remained below 1995 levels.
"Hajdutej's sales in 1996 were in harmony with expectations," Joep Cheriex, chairman of the board and Jeroen van Douveren, member of the board, said in Hajdutej's earnings report.
Hajdutej's domestic sales rose by 18.7 percent, while its exports grew by 36.2 percent.
Operating profit of Hajdutej, which is majority-owned by Nutricia of the Netherlands, remained below that in 1995.
"Operating profit fell due to a sharp decline in export subsidies and also because a substantial one-of cost in the second half of the year," they said.
Hajdutej's operating profit shrank to 49.6 million forints in 1996 on sales of 11.32 billion from an operating profit of 173.9 million on sales of 9.28 billion in 1995.
The company swung to a net loss of 5.3 million forints from a net profit of 117.8 million in 1995.
"If export subsidies in 1996 had remained at the 1995 levels, operating profits in 1996 would have been 224 million forints," Hajdutej said.
The company said the board was optimistic that 1997 will bring better results.
"Unless unexpected developments occur, the board expects results to improve in this financial year and expects the results to reflect reorganisation and its positive impacts," the company said.
